title: new03, rtree arm -- same bug, second observable
live_proof: inspection in the 3.22.0 tree: nodeNew() allocates the RtreeNode and its payload as one block with pNode->zData pointing inside it, nodeWrite() binds that payload SQLITE_STATIC into the cached pWriteNode statement, and sqlite3_reset() does not clear bindings. Fixed upstream in 3.23.0 (eab0e10304), sixteen days after 3.22.0 shipped, by adding the missing bind_null
object: the RtreeNode payload buffer, still bound as parameter 2 of a persistent cached statement
lifetime_ender: nodeRelease() frees the node block while the cached statement's binding still points into it
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator. Same upstream fix as case 19 and deliberately kept separate (corrected 2026-10-16: this said case 20, which is d4b646997a and unrelated; the renumber from 38 cases to 33 on 2026-10-06 left both halves of this pair pointing at the wrong row): one upstream commit, two independently reachable observables, in rtree and in fts3. The threat model is upstream's own, quoted in the fix's commit message: a caller may reach the persistent statement through sqlite3_next_stmt() and read the freed buffer. One part of the trigger is ours and is declared here: before the re-step it asks memsys5 for blocks of the node payload size and fills them with 0x5A, so that the freed block is reclaimed and the consequence is deterministic. Without it the re-step still reads through the dangling binding -- Sublet faults on it with cause 25 and probe site 56 witnesses it -- but the bytes it copies are usually the node's own, so the row is rewritten unchanged and the data loss cannot be shown: measured 2026-10-16, both virtual arms came back rows_lost=0 and the case printed its own note saying the block had not been reused. The binding, the free and the re-step are untouched by it

sublet.oracle: VM HALTED on a capability fault, cause 24 untagged dereference (temporal: revoked, or never a capability) pc=0x800239e4 -- taken outside the domain, so cooperative recovery has no frame to return through; all 28 halts in this arm are at the same kernel pc 0x800239e4

status: re-measured 2026-10-16 on this platform, on a trigger that is now one file for all arms (see note), and no verdict changes. virtual-malloc MISSED, RETURNED, both controls as declared, and it now shows the consequence it previously could not: first4 0x00000031 -> 0x5A5A5A5A, scan_after=ERROR(query failed), rows_lost=ALL(scan failed) was 120, marker_in_row=1. virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT, cause=25 pc=0x3f848020f8 offset 204 in memcpy at fault address 0x3f9af79980, inside the arena, both controls as declared; it faults at the stale read and never reaches the VERDICT line. cheribsd-revocation MISSED, RETURNED rc=0, the same data loss, PRAGMA integrity_check rc=0, with the boot's positive control trapping and revocation knobs 1/0. host ASan is the 2026-10-11 bundle's reading and was taken on the PRE-UNIFICATION trigger -- READ of size 820, 40 bytes into a freed 864-byte region, sqlite3VdbeSerialPut <- sqlite3VdbeExec <- sqlite3_step, freed by nodeRelease <- rtreeUpdate, allocated by nodeAcquire -- and could not be re-run because this host has no x86 ASan runtime. The change only adds allocations before the re-step, so the access it reports is the same instruction on the same object, and the three arms' re-measurement establishes the access independently. The arms block is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16; every verdict holds and no count moves. Three things are corrected. (1) The two copies of the trigger were different programs, and the corpus one could not demonstrate its own consequence. ports/sqlite/cheribsd/cases/case_rtree_static_bind.c carried a documented deviation -- 16 sqlite3_malloc calls of node size, filled with 0x5A, before the re-step -- because on purecap the freed block was not being reused and the copy was a no-op. The corpus copy had no such step, and on both virtual arms it measured rows_lost=0 with the case's own note 'the freed block had not been reused yet'. The reclaim step is now part of the corpus case.c and the CheriBSD copy is that file byte for byte, as case 02's was; neither reason ports/sqlite/cheribsd/port.json gives for the two sets differing applies here, since this case opens :memory: and the step is trigger, not probe. On the unified trigger all three arms show the same consequence. (2) Two defects in that step are fixed. It hardcoded the request as page_size-64 = 960, but iNodeSize is 820 here: getNodeSize clamps it so at most RTREE_MAXCELLS=51 cells fit, 4+51*16. It worked only because memsys5 rounds 960 and sizeof(RtreeNode)+820 into the same size class, so the size is now taken from the node payload length the case has just measured. And its recovered_freed_node check compared a fresh allocation's first four bytes against the node's, which cannot ever match -- memsys5 has already written Mem5Link{next,prev} over the freed block's first eight bytes -- so it printed 'no' on runs where the marker did reach the row; recovery is now reported by marker_in_row, which is the check that can fire. (3) The attribution is no longer 'any memcpy would count'. Probe site 56 prints the pointer at the SQLITE_STATIC bind in nodeWrite, at the free in nodeRelease and at the copy in sqlite3VdbeSerialPut, and the three are one value: BIND zData=0x21e440 node=0x21e400, FREE node=0x21e400 zData=0x21e440, then after the re-step marker SERIAL z=0x21e440 len=820 first4=0x5a5a5a5a. The content is the second, independent argument: 0x5A5A5A5A can only have come from the block after it was freed and reclaimed. Recorded about the probe itself: the address judgement gets this case wrong in both configurations. On virtual-malloc the block is still free at the read, so it reports kind=UAF off=64 n=820 req=1024 and off=64 is exactly sizeof(RtreeNode) under the 16-byte-pointer layout, confirming zData == &pNode[1]. On CheriBSD the block has been reclaimed by the trigger's own 0x5A allocation, and the read of 820 bytes from offset 64 runs past that allocation's 820 requested bytes, so it reports kind=OOB -- an artifact of the request size, not an over-read, the same misclassification case 09 had to correct. Before the request size was fixed it reported nothing at all (hits=197, witnesses=0). The witness does corroborate identity from the other side: its blk=0x21e400 is the node pointer the bind and free hooks recorded
fault_sites_why: The cached statement's parameter still points into the freed node; stepping it copies the binding in sqlite3VdbeSerialPut (consumer), with memcpy. Weaker than a single function: any memcpy under it would count. Declared 2026-10-10 after the virtual runs resolved faults there; the reason is the source and PROVENANCE.md cited, which predate those runs. STRENGTHENED 2026-10-16 by probe site 56, which replaces the function-level claim with pointer identity: the pointer nodeWrite binds SQLITE_STATIC, the pointer nodeRelease frees, and the pointer sqlite3VdbeSerialPut copies out of are printed at all three hooks and are one value, on native memsys5 and on CheriBSD purecap alike. The memcpy Sublet faults in is therefore the one reading the freed node payload, and not any other memcpy under the statement. The length agrees too: len=820 at the copy is the node payload size, and the probe's off=64 is sizeof(RtreeNode) under this ABI.
